_README: Config for reward-guard.sh on CheffyLinux (bazzite/KDE). While the Reward Vault has NO active timer, any process whose executable path is under blockPaths (or whose name is in blockProcessNames) is killed, unless spared by allowPaths/allowProcessNames. Any active reward timer (all 3 tiers) unlocks everything. Only games are killed - the network is never touched. Paths may start with ~ (expands to your home). After editing, reload: systemctl --user restart reward-guard
_blockPaths_note: Native Steam only (confirmed no Flatpak Steam on this box) - single library at ~/.local/share/Steam. If you add another library later (external drive/SD card), check ~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf and add its .../steamapps/common path here. ~/Games covers Lutris's default install location (Lutris is installed here) - adjust/remove if you install Lutris games to a different folder. ~/Faugus is Faugus Launcher's default Wine-prefix root (its PREFIXES_DIR) - Battle.net and every game it in turn launches (Overwatch, Diablo, WoW, etc.) all run inside the same prefix under here, and any other non-Steam game added in Faugus gets its own subfolder here too, so this one entry covers all of it. If Settings -> 'Default Prefixes Location' in Faugus was changed from the default, update this to match (or add the custom path in addition).
_blockProcessNames_note: Killed by process name (as seen in /proc/<pid>/comm, 15-char Linux limit) wherever it runs - covers FFXIV played through XIVLauncher (installed here as the dev.goats.xivlauncher Flatpak) and Battle.net, where the real game executable is hidden inside a Wine/Proton prefix. Faugus/Battle.net games are also matched by WINEPREFIX now (see blockPaths' ~/Faugus entry), which covers every Battle.net game generically - these two entries are just a name-based backstop for the launcher itself. If FFXIV or the launcher doesn't die when locked, run `ps -eo pid,comm | grep -i xiv` (or `battle`) while it's running and add whatever name shows up.
_allowPaths_note: Non-game software living under a blockPath, plus productivity 'games' to keep runnable even with no timer. wallpaper_engine matches the Steam app you have installed.
